answer: Canary-trap attestations: each identity locks a bond that is a bridge to payouts — rewards cross only after passing hidden checks. The jury seeds the pool with traps tagged with an umber mark in its ledger. A faker with n identities can't tell real tasks from traps, so each clone must complete every trap itself; one forged record can't cover two clones, each facing its own gauntlet. Cost scales superlinearly: n clones need n bonds and n full trap histories, nothing amortizable. One tripped canary drops that clone's bond to its nadir: total loss. Honest agents cross their bridges untouched.
